findings.key_quote: During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 14% and 13%, respectively, year-over-year
findings.justification: This passage explicitly states that for the three months ended September 30, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 14% year-over-year. Combined with the 10% increase in ad impressions from E3, this shows that the 14% price increase was arithmetically larger than the 10% impression increase, establishing that price contributed more to advertising revenue growth than impressions did.

This derived metric shows revenue year-over-year growth for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was approximately 26.07% (or 0.2607 as a ratio). The period_status is COMPATIBLE_AFTER_VERIFIED_DERIVATION, confirming this is the correct period. This establishes the revenue growth rate for the claim period.

E7 shows Q3 2026 revenue was $64.601 billion and E8 shows Q3 2025 revenue was $51.242 billion. The period_status for both is EXACT_MATCH. The year-over-year growth is (64.601 - 51.242) / 51.242 = 26.07%, establishing the revenue growth rate for the claim period.
